why: A = Euclidean version plus manifold version, each assuming only that f is C² at p (not smooth everywhere), with no Hausdorff hypothesis, any universe, and an iff conclusion. B assumes f is C^∞ on all of M, M Hausdorff, in Type. So A ⇒ B directly (specialize the manifold conjunct). B ⇒ A would need the C²-at-p, non-T2 case and the Euclidean conjunct for functions that are not globally smooth. That is a genuine difference in hypotheses, not a gap in proof effort.
